subject: Post-call recap: AcmeHealth - Private/VPC deployment requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Khan <sara.khan@acmehealth.com>, Brian Turner <brian.turner@acmehealth.com>
Cc: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: AcmeHealth - Private/VPC deployment requirements

Hi Sara / Brian —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Key Pain Points (as discussed)
- Data residency: AcmeHealth requires all PHI/PII to remain in US East regions and a customer-controlled VPC.
- Network restrictions: No inbound internet access to the model hosts; egress must be via customer-managed NAT or proxy.
- Air-gap / regulated environments: Some of your clinics will require an air-gapped option for offline inference.
- Audit & key management: KMS/HSM integration and detailed audit logs (token-level + request traces) are mandatory.

Goals
- Proof-of-concept (POC) running on AcmeHealth-managed VPC in AWS us-east-1 with sample dataset (non-production) by end of Q3.
- Define procurement/compliance checklist and timeline for a production roll in Q4.

What Redwood can provide (high-level)
- Private deployment package: control plane subscription with customer VPC connectors and optional on-prem package for air-gapped sites.
- KMS/HSM integration, SOC 2 evidence, and per-request audit logs.
- Network checklist for firewall/NAT/proxy and port requirements.

Immediate next steps
1) I’ll share: (a) high-level architecture diagram, (b) network requirements template, (c) SOC2 summary. 
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra/security team — propose Thu 7/16 or Mon 7/20, 10-11am ET.
3) Draft a 6-week mutual action plan for the POC once we confirm the deep-dive attendees.

Attachments: redwood-private-overview.pdf, network-requirements-template.xlsx, soc2-report-summary.pdf

Let me know if I missed anything important. Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0184

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the summary — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifying questions before we schedule the deep-dive: 

1) For the air-gapped option, can Redwood confirm whether the on-prem package supports offline model updates (we will need to push model updates via removable media under controlled procedures)?  
2) Narrowing down the network checklist: do you require specific outbound ports to Redwood control plane for telemetry, or is a full offline mode supported where telemetry is buffered locally and uploaded manually?

If you can flag who on your engineering team can join the deep dive (SE + infra contact), that’ll help us invite the right folks. Proposed deep-dive times on our side: Thu 7/16 13:00-14:00 ET or Mon 7/20 10:00-11:00 ET.

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Brian Turner <brian.turner@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: AcmeHealth - Private/VPC deployment requirements

Hi Brian —

Thanks for the great questions. Quick technical answers below; happy to cover in the deep-dive.

1) Air-gapped/on-prem model updates:
- Our on-prem air-gap option supports offline updates. We provide a signed artifact bundle that can be transferred on removable media. The bundle includes model binaries, manifest, and signed checksums; install requires SE assistance for integrity verification.

2) Telemetry / control-plane connectivity:
- We support two modes:
  a) Connected mode (recommended POC): Lightweight telemetry and health checks to Redwood control plane over TLS. All telemetry can be routed through customer-managed NAT/proxy.
  b) Fully offline mode: Telemetry is buffered locally and exported via signed bundles for manual upload. In offline mode, certain features (auto-scaling, remote rollouts) are disabled.

Network specifics (summary) — see attached network-requirements-template.xlsx for full port/protocol list, but high level:
- Outbound TLS (443) to control plane endpoints (configurable by FQDN / IP allowlist).
- Optional: allow outbound to S3 endpoints if you want remote model staging.
- For air-gapped installs: HTTPS egress can be blocked; we’ll rely on manual artifact transfer.

Who will join from our side for the deep-dive:
- Dylan Brooks (Solutions Engineer) — dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
- Marissa Cole (AE) — marissa.cole@redwood.ai
- Monica Patel (Sales Engineering Lead) — monica.patel@redwood.ai (cc’d)

I’ll attach the SOC2 summary and a short architecture sketch to this thread. Happy to do Thu 7/16 13:00 ET (your 1pm) — works for our team.

Cheers,
Dylan
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
